I'm sorry to have to write a negative review for this game but I find this game in many ways as frustrating as playing the NHL franchise.

First of, there are lots of game breaking bugs and freezes. These get patched over time of course but they do ruin a lot of experience when they happen. The game freezes at different points and you have to force restart, losing progress. I also believe there is some memory leak because if you play several games in a row, without restarting, the players start twitching and the controls aren't as responsive.

For the more important big picture stuff: the game is just frustrating to play due to how the AI behaves and how the AI cheats. This is similar to the NHL franchise. If you go up in difficulty the AI doesn't become smarter, it just gets a bunch of advantages.

One example is that you can no longer pass a puck through an opponent. Of course in some situations that makes sense, but when you are setting up a breakaway and the opponent right next to you, facing another direction, intercepts your pass easily it becomes very frustrating. The thing is that your own players are way worse at interceptions. That's generally the theme, that your teammates are crap while the opponents are superstars (which I mean is technically true since half your team is made up of benchwarmers, but that's still a problem with the game).

Another example is that the opposing goalie grows into a wall at times. It literally feels like your playing against a wall because your players keep on shooting open netters back into the goalie. Another thing is that the game seems scripted at times, like the NHL franchise. A good example of both these things is one game I played against the Meatballs I think it was. I played a solid first period, scoring a goal early. Then in the last half a minute or so of the first period the other team just rattled of 4 goals in a row, most of them softies. I got frustrated but went into the second period giving it my all. Somehow I managed to score 3 goals and tie it 4-4 for OT. I then went onto to dominate the OT completely... but I still lost because their goalie kept on making ridiculous 2 on 0 saves like it was somehow predetermined. Eventually they scored on a softy. At that point the shots were something like 76-32 in my favor.

Another thing that I find frustrating is how easy it is to check my own teammates. It happens way too often that I aim for an opponent (and seemingly hit them) but somehow my teammate is the one falling down. I'm also not sure if it's scripted this way, but this happens so often when I try to check the "king" with his slapper. [spoiler] For those that don't know the king will wind up a slapper from the blueline. It will score 100% of the time. [/spoiler] He is, however, very easy to check to the ground... except when he's standing there. This might be a skill issue on my part but somehow in that situation I always end up checking down my own players right next to him. I maybe hit 80% of my hits and that's when the opponents are moving, but this guy standing still I only manage to hit 20% of the time. 

Yet another example that goes to show the asymmetrical AI is the Meatball team again. They have a forward always lurking around my blueline. That's fine of course. I don't mind that my teammates are all in the offensive zone because that's part of the challenge. However, you can get this talent as well on your team. You can have one player lurking on their blueline. But what happens then? They place one of their defenseman next to him. That's quite unfair, that my teammates are stupider than the opponents. It seems to be a general trend.

One thing that is not directly related to AI but to aiming is the aim assist for passes (and probably for shots as well) is oftentimes poor. A good example of this is when I was setting up a forward for a breakout by aiming up along the boards. What happened instead? The puck was passed to the opponent in front of the net who scored. That only happened once but a thing that happens all the time is that I aim to pass for a teammate on a cross crease but instead it's picked up by another teammate further back.

I've gone over the frustration with the AI. Another thing is that the roguelike aspect is not that great. The same thing happens on each run. I get that the team is small and content takes time, but I would have liked more randomness in what happens. The most frustrating experience is playing the football team. Facing "Leo Messier" and an 11 man squad was hilarious the first time it happened, but it wore out its welcome quickly. This is a hockey game. I don't want to play football. Getting through that team is such a drag, especially with the AI issues listed above. Could we please only get to play the football team once every 10 times?

I'll wrap up with the parts I like. The game has lots of great humor. It looks great. Just jumping into a single game and playing against an equally talented AI team is quite fun. A lot of the abilities in the game are quite well thought out (even though they can be quite unbalanced and some of them don't seem to have much effect).

This game has a lot of promise but I cannot recommend it to anyone in its current form. With enough playtime the poor design is impossible to ignore and becomes the focus.

The core hockey game in Tape to Tape is mostly fine. There's still some major control issues - infuriating goalie AI, bad passing and player switch controls (neither the switch button nor joystick directional controls on controller remedy the problem, which is that you need to be able to reliably switch to specific characters if you want the ability system to mean anything on defense) - all of which will need to be tuned or reworked before launch. Adding some additional defensive options like a player dive has been noted by many already and is direly needed even if the poor defensive switching controls will limit its use.

The biggest problems here are in the roguelike elements of the core gameplay loop, which in current iteration are drastically unbalanced, more frustrating than fun and not particularly well thought out. Some very simple needed conveniences are missing - for example, a number of events involve Angus taking on a perk with a benefit and drawback. How about the "skip" button most modern roguelikes/roguelites offer so the player isn't forced to take on a drawback that damages their strategy for that run? Besides some possible early high rolls, the core loop has derailed my runs far more than it has enhanced them. Many times the reward for a sudden death "hallway fight" is being forced to take a bad perk that might be good in a certain context. Numerous times I've had 3 "trait" options that were all actively bad for my players with no option to skip and boy does that destroy whatever fun I was having building my team. There needs to be a lot less "this relic sucks but it's good if you have this other relic" type combination shenanigans when lowrolling early on Expert means you're probably gonna have a tough enough time with that first elite. In the current iteration of the game there is simply not enough rewards through a run to expect players to hit on relic/ability synergies with any consistency so be mindful of the amount of duds. The design decisions around the core gameplay loop made this game completely unenjoyable after enough iterations.

The unlocks on the roguelite side are quite frustrating too. You will unlock plenty of characters and skills and find them nearly useless, clogging up your start of game RNG, wishing you hadn't wasted your rubber on making your core gameplay loop worse. How about the ability to take unlocks out of the pool with a simple deselect in the shop menu? After about 25 hours I felt I had to wipe my save file to redo my unlocks to be more competitive in Expert. Losing out on "additional run variety" doesn't seem like a great argument considering the quality of some of the skills, not to mention how purely defensive skills are held back by the aforementioned lack of precise player switching.

Overall: the hockey loop is pretty fun but needs some major improvements to have replay-ability which seems pretty important for a game based on a short gameplay loop. Roguelike elements desperately need a rework if the current gameplay loop is intended to be the core. The idea of a "roguelike hockey" game is full of potential but the current offering remains too half-baked. The gameplay loop is addictive but the current balancing of skills, characters and elites is so poor I would legitimately recommend avoiding playing much until more considerable updates are made.

I think this game could be really good and really fun. I still think there are a lot of problems though. Most of them were covered in Triceraclopse's review so I will try to just keep it brief.

1) The teammate AI specifically for where you are on an odd man rush is annoying. Most the time your teammates will just keep skating to the goal line or go really wide out to the boards, which puts them in horrible position to actually score goals. It would be better if they would stop at the top of the circle or in the slot for a one timer. This especially can be a problem when the players in the odd man rush have vastly different speeds.

2) Expert mode sucks. Your teammate AI is way to bad to help play defense and your goalie isn't good enough to make up for them. In addition to that, scoring should definitely be harder than in standard mode, but once you get to the end of the first act, it feels more like luck than anything to score. You can have a cross ice pass to someone with 65 shot power and accuracy and the one-timer will still be saved all the time. The only way I've found to score is to have someone with the rebound magnet skill and the behavior that makes them stay in front of the net and just keep shooting for rebounds. But to get that combination is pretty difficult and it still doesn't get you that far.

3) I don't know if this is just cause the game is early access, but it feels like there really isn't enough to the campaign for how much there is to unlock. After a while it just becomes pretty stagnant and the only way I could see someone wanting to 100% it is because they are a completionist. Roguelites should make you want to replay it over and over. Maybe if there were more games in each world and a much larger variety of teams that you randomly play against I could see it being more fun. But for now it just feels like every run is the same.

4) Backwards skating w/o the puck is so stiff. It feels like you can only face one direction, and imo there is no reason to ever skate backwards because skating forwards is just always a better option. My suggestion here is to first make it so when you are skating backwards on defense, you just face the opposite direction of your movement. As someone who played hockey for a long time, it feels weird to just not be able to do that. Also probably just make the backwards skating a little faster.

5) Switching characters and passing to a specific target feels kind of clunky. Attempting a pass across the ice when in the offensive zone is almost impossible since the center is always just parked in between. This becomes a big deal if one of your characters passes cant be intercepted cause then you're really not able to make the one pass you really want to make. As for switching characters, it feels impossible sometimes to get to the specific person you want to switch to.

6) Sometimes when you shoot, you lose control of the character for a while after. I don't know if this is on purpose but it makes it hard to shoot and then go get the rebound if you're not automatically switched to a different player.

Like I said, this game is still a lot of fun. I would just wait for it to find its sweet spot.

At first glance, this game really feels it has hit the mark with a refreshing yet nostalgic take on the genre. However, the "roguelike" elements are really a disguise for what is completely imbalanced NPC gameplay and unfair game mechanics (especially once you enter the "Expert" difficulty). 

A few examples:
- Passes ignoring input and going to the incorrect teammate in order to force a turnover
- Altered stats on your players so that they are weaker/slower than vs. previous opponents
- NPC teammate movement away from the puck designed to make passing impossible or create turnovers
- Opponent passing/reaction time that far exceeds that of a human player
- Power-up use that benefits the opponent (ref superstar's whistle causing "turnovers" which are really passes to the opponent)

Simply put, there's a deep need for compelling and challenging gameplay that is based on proper game design and not cheap tactics/game-breaking mechanics. This game does not have that. I will not be returning to this game without a major overhaul to the game mechanics.

[Edit after Sep 15, 2023 update]
The game has finally received an update which supposedly changed much of the AI and game mechanics. However, a recent play-through confirms that the game is still marred by all of the criticism I previously wrote. They disguise a variable opponent difficulty as part of the roguelite experience, but it's not actually related to any statistics or power-ups. Instead, the game can and will become more difficult at any time in your run, completely obliterating any consistency in opponent from one run to the next. And ultimately, you WILL fail many more times than not. A successful run on Expert difficulty, in turn, is predicated on receiving the perfect mix of power-ups that finally make you OP enough to have a slim opportunity to get past the AI's unreal skill ceiling and inhuman abilities. Even then, you are likely to fail to the final boss team.

The recent updates appear to have kept all of this inconsistency in the game (as I truly believe the designers feel it is a "feature" of their game), while upping the difficulty of opponent goaltenders and AI. Simply put, this is a complete step in the wrong direction without addressing any of the existing problems.

[Edit after Oct 2025 update]
Sad to report that all of the same problems explained above still persist, despite a massive overhaul to the game with many new additions. Unfortunately, none of this makes the game worth playing when there are still obvious issues with both the AI of your opponents and your teammates. This game could be great but the devs refuse to acknowledge and fix the actual problems with gameplay.

I really didn't want to leave a negative review because the demo had me so excited for this release, but I feel like I have to. In concept, its an arcade-style sports game (like NBA Street or NFL Blitz), combined with the charm of the old backyard sports games (Pablo 4ever), and with roguelite features mixed in. I love the game in concept... in execution it has flaws that are incredibly annoying. As such, I cannot recommend this game in its current state. It has to many bad design choices that make the game less fun.

Firstly, the more things you unlock, the less likely to get any one thing you have unlocked when you start a new run. You only get three choices. The result? You dilute your power and superstar pool with trash and have to start with things you don't want to play with. That is a punishment for unlocking things. Not a reward.

Here's a for instance: I unlocked a magnet power for 30 rubber [strike](which by the way, takes a long time to accumulate)[/strike]. I'd love to play with the magnet I spent all my rubber on, but 5 runs later it hasn't come up. So I spent 30 rubber on an item I don't actually get to use. That is an example of how roguelite features are treated in this game. They make the game less fun. If I unlock something you should let me pick it, especially if you are going to force me to grind currency to unlock it. Give me other incentives to play with the substandard powers and superstars but don't punish me for progress.

The most optimal strategy for playing this game would be, to spend all your rubber on improving McShaggy's stats early because you have to play with him every run. DO NOT pay rubber to unlock anything else until you figure out what you actually want to play with. Then once you've seen something in game that you think you would like to play with, spend rubber to unlock it. This is a perverse incentive, and it is not fun. Never unlock a bad superstar or bad power, because if you do, it will become part of your pool forever.

Other "features" that are not fun: 
1) I have rolled the same 3 superstars choices 4 runs in a row even though I have 6 available. That isn't fun. I want to try different superstars. 

2) The benchwarmers you start with are very bad, and they are given randomly.  You aren't going very far in a run where all your benchwarmers have sub 20 speed. They are too slow to handle the puck, and the CPU can easily skate around them when they are on defense. A player with sub-20 speed is basically unusable.

3) Why is the player goalie AI so terrible? Why is the goalie not upgradeable? I don't get to control him so it would be nice if I could make him better somehow. This problem is magnified by the simple fact that your goalie sucks and the other team's goalie is a god. It makes you feel like a slave to RNG. Yes, I know there are some events that affect your goalie, but they mostly just break him and make him worse. He can't pass at all. You are better off just covering the puck everytime and going to a faceoff.

4) Events are almost always more negative than positive. It is better to just avoid them... this is poor design. I understand the need for risk/reward, but the reward seems very low, which typically is a talent you could just pick up from the "score the first goal" game (and there you actually get a choice). The difference being that these "rewards" always come with a big stat hit or some other ailment that makes the player, on balance, worse. You also don't get to select who gets it. The game picks for you. Bad all around. Better off playing the talent game or going to the campfire and taking stats. This is almost always the case.

5) I don't want to post any spoilers but some of the later encounters have so much crap going on that they aren't fun. The enemy team just spamming superstar powers (because all 5 of them have them), while your stick flies out of your hand on every shot. Some of the powers are not avoidable. There were points in those games where my entire team was disabled in some way or another, and I literally didn't have a player I could control. I just got to watch the other team tee off on my goalie until they scored. Taking agency away from the player is not good game design. It didn't even feel like I was playing a hockey game in these encounters. I am not sure what it was, but it wasn't good. This needs to be fixed.

6) The hitbox for checking the CPU is inconsistent at best. If your players get breathed on they lose the puck. If they happen to actually get touched, they are down for what seems like an eternity. When you try to check? The other team frequently will just run right through you even when you have defensive talents and a high checking stat. 

7) Teammate AI is pretty awful. On defense your players just sort of collect in front of the net and stand there hoping to be hit with a puck. On offense they frequently get in your way instead of trying to find open ice where you can pass them the puck. Of all my complaints, I'd say this one is the least important. You can learn to play around bad teammate AI. You can even enjoy it if the rest of the game is good. The problem is, that I just don't feel like it is.

I really wanted to like this game. I hope the devs read this and address some of these items because I want to enjoy playing this game and I want this game to succeed. I think it could be amazing.

Edit: I have written some suggestions I believe would greatly improve the game.

My suggestions?

1) Allow the player to select whichever unlocked superstar power they want OR take a random unlocked power with a bonus.

2) Allow the player to select the Superstar teammate they want OR take a random + bonus.

3) Allow the player to have some impact on the benchwarmers they get. Whether its a choice of team style (speed, defensive, offensive) or select the individual benchwarmers from the bench warmer pool (this can be randomly determined). This ensures you don't get three players with sub-20 speed (I would argue that none of the players should have speed that low because it makes them completely useless).

4) Rework the second boss. It isn't fun or fair. Superstar powers need longer cooldowns. CPUs should not be able to off screen you with their powers. Certain powers should probably be removed completely (I am looking at you, block of ice).

[strike]5) Increase the number of rubbers the player receives from wins, and award a small amount in a loss.[/strike] The amount of rubber awarded was increased via patch. I no longer have any complaints about the amount of rubber awarded per run.

6) Do something with the goalie. Its literally your most important defender and integral to hockey and it is an afterthought in this game.

I really want to recommend this game as a hockey fan, but I just can't in its current state. It certainly has its moments, and it [i] almost [/i] has that addictive quality that great roguelikes have, but it has some absolute glaring issues that make it incredibly frustrating to play beyond Act 1. 

[b] Issue #1: The AI [/b] 
The teammate AI is a mixed bag. In some ways it works well; it's clear that effort was taken to ensure that it plays well in the offensive zone, with the AI-controlled players reliably getting in position to receive cross-seam passes. The issues with the AI become more obvious when you don't have the puck. The AI seems to have no concept of "last man back", and will charge straight towards the puck carrier in the neutral zone. This frequently gives your opponent scoring chances, and I'd wager at least half of the goals I allowed were scored at least in part due to this. 
The other annoying issue is how bad the AI is at moving to get the puck. The bots aren't very good at predicting where the puck is going, often completely missing what should be an easy rebound to bang home. This is compounded by how awkward it is to pick up bouncing pucks. 

[b] Issue #2: The Opponents [/b] 
The early opponents are just basic teams with simple themes. As the run progresses, the opponents get more varied and interesting, but also much worse to play against. In Act 3, teams are spamming their special abilities so much it becomes impossible to play with any strategy or skill; I beat the 'final boss' team by just dumping the puck and trying to win the faceoff. This is boring, but anything else is nearly impossible because otherwise your players are more often than not knocked out. These teams should provide a challenge, but are really just a slog. 

[b] Issue #3: The Progression [/b]
Tape to Tape draws massive inspiration from Slay the Spire, but seems to completely miss what makes that game so addictive. In StS, winning a run with a character unlocks the next level of Ascension for that character, which is essentially a slightly-harder version of the run you just beat. As the player improves, the game offers harder and harder challenges to match them, which makes them want to keep coming back for 'one more run.' In Tape to Tape, you get currency to buy upgrades between runs to make the game easier, which kills the feeling of wanting to come back to do it all over again. 

[b] Issue #4: The Content [/b] 
I can cut the game some slack as an early access indie title, but that doesn't change the fact there's just not enough content for the price right now. You play almost the exact same teams in the exact same order every time. Other roguelikes like StS put players into completely different builds and scenarios every run, but Tape to Tape starts to feels repetitive after just a few hours. There's a decent variety of starting abilities for the player to use, but they're mostly totally useless by Act 3 anyway. 

So yeah. I want to love this game, but it's incredibly frustrating and repetitive in it's current state. Losing runs rarely felt like the consequence of a mistake but instead the result of janky mechanics or pure RNG (I once outshot an opponent 25-to-1 and lost...) I sincerely hope these issues are addressed, because the core of this game could be awesome if it were improved upon further.

I really wanted to like this game. I've always loved 2D hockey games and have played a lot of rogue-likes over the years. I really like the general art style, music (although it definitely gets repetitive), and the sound design is really good. The gameplay reminds me a lot of old school hockey games with a modern feel. I had a dozen or so hours of fun out of the game, so if you think that's worth it at this price point, it's worth the price.

TL;DR: I like a lot about the game and I wish I could have enjoyed it for longer but there are issues. The game goes from impossibly easy to impossibly hard very quickly and it stops feeling rewarding once you realize how weak most of the unlocks are. Player AI is objectively horrible in 'Expert' difficulty and the game gets stale as a result.

Now for the massive rants

1) [b] Gameplay Loop [/b] 

Very similar to other rogue-likes; you play out a run until the run ends at a final boss or you die to one of the other bosses, and then you earn currency (pucks) to upgrade your character, unlocks, etc. for your next run to make it a little easier. Unfortunately, 90% of the power and superstar unlocks make your runs harder. One of the worst powers in the game is locked behind a 200 puck investment (roughly 2 runs of currency) that WILL lose you games, and therefore runs if you try to use it. You get the best power in the game without investing anything and arguably only 1 or 2 other powers are even worth using. Secondly, the character unlocks seem like wasted potential - they have the same power options (with the exception of two) and generally speaking, the reason certain ones are better are their stats, which would be fine if all stats were equally weighted (more on that later).

2) [b] Difficulty Curve [/b] 

The game defaults to standard, which, if you've played a few hours, quickly becomes pretty easy. It's not like you win every run, but you'll consistently get the last act. However, once you beat a run, you'll unlock 'Expert Mode'! Based on the description, you'll have to apply both build knowledge and good hockey mechanics to win, right? Well no. You'll pretty much have to pray to get lucky on a mix of AI, item unlocks, and a good power/superstar within your first few games of the run or the run will end on a boss pretty consistently. For context, I've beaten standard ~4-5 times in standard and after dozens of expert runs, I have only gotten past the first act once. No, I'm not losing to an unfair boss every time - I'm losing to one of the first two bosses because their players are not only higher stats, talent-boosted, but they're also way more coordinated than I literally ever could be due to AI.

3) [b] Player AI [/b]

At first, I thought my lack of success in Expert was just a skill issue so I decided to actually record a few of my runs to see if I felt like I was missing obvious shot opportunities, etc. but nope, the game just never gave me any from its AI, so most of my goals (if I get any) are lucky breakaway goals or cheesy goals using certain powers (which are inconsistent to say the least). The player AI for defense is even worse, for one, they will ALWAYS go for the puck (at least 1, if not more) if you don't have control of the puck, even if you are less than a foot away from it. Secondly, they straight up stop poke checking in Expert, even though they do obsessively in Standard. Lastly, the player goalie feels extremely gimped compared to enemy goalie. I have tons of games where I lost even with twice the amount of shots because the enemy AI not only will execute incredibly coordinated plays and get a goal (fair) but also get random trash goals from the blue line (way too often).

4) [b] Flawed Mechanics [/b]

I could write a lot about this but this rant is already too long. In short, certain stats are just OBJECTIVELY better, even if you get the perfect cards/etc. for focusing on another stat. I'll give two examples of a build I had success with and a build that will almost always die (even in Standard) due to certain boss mechanics. These will contain heavy spoilers.

[spoiler] Speed Focused Builds [/spoiler]
[spoiler] Art imitates life I guess, right? Well in Tape to Tape speed and accuracy are king. Yes, you can probably cheese out a run with a super OP checking build but it is way way easier to win on speed/accuracy builds largely because they can confuse the AI enough that you will win most runs, especially on Standard, if you get lucky with speed-focused talents and accuracy/shot manipulation talents. I think it's logical that speed is [i] strong [/i] but should it really be [i] outright better [/i] than any other type of build? [/spoiler]

[spoiler] Checking Focused Builds [/spoiler]
[spoiler] Man these are fun, which is a shame because they really suck at winning runs. I've had a build where my entire team had spiked armor (makes you immune to being hit), 80+ checking, and even a superstar point shooter but nope I couldn't score a goal to save my life because the AI is too good against point shooters (and terrible against cross-crease breakaway goals). I have even tried sacking a player (they play stickless and knock people over) and just stacking checking to see how far I could go, but alas I lost the cultists because they're generally hard to score against. [/spoiler]

Yes, most well-crafted builds can win in Standard but this isn't even remotely true for Expert. The furthest I went in Expert was primarily because of a good mix of good friendly AI and poor enemy AI (enemy goalkeeper straight up said no and left in overtime).

[b] Final Thoughts [/b]
I've definitely overwritten this review and I really do wish I could recommend this game but unfortunately I don't think this game is living up to its potential. The bad AI, and general difficulty curve could be massively improved if friendly AI was at least similar in complexity to enemy AI but this doesn't seem like something that will be easily fixed. Additionally, if I could at least view the enemy roster to see what skills/talents/powers they have that's causing them to beat me so consistently (in Expert), I could maybe feel better prepared to play against their strengths if I even knew what was happening. Generally, I think some of the powers ([spoiler] Dragon Shout, Yo-Yo, Headbasher, Dance, Grapple, Slow Time [/spoiler]) could be buffed and it would at least feel better to unlock them. I would kind like to play a difficulty in between Standard and Expert to make the curve a little more rounded. And lastly, could we split the difference in stats [i] somewhat [/i] between superstars and benchwarmers a little so I could at least clear the first couple bosses more consistently in Expert without feeling like I'm playing 2 v 5?
